== Course of events ==

Having endured a series of peculiar encounters—from the White Rabbit's mistaken commands to the Pigeon's fearful accusations about her serpent-like form—Alice finds herself speaking with a singular Caterpillar about her present circumstances. She complains of her height: at three inches tall, she is distressingly small in this bewildering realm where size seems to shift without reason or warning. Yet the Caterpillar, who happens to be precisely three inches high himself, meets her complaint with a steadfast declaration. He proclaims that three inches is a good height—a perfectly respectable measure, in his estimation—and assures her that she will adjust to it with time.

This exchange embodies the strange wisdom of Wonderland, where the Caterpillar's own modest stature grants him an air of authority on the matter. His reassurance offers little solace to Alice's distress, for it rests upon an assumption that her adaptation is not merely possible but inevitable, as if such upheaval were a small matter of patience rather than a fundamental transformation of her person.
